answer: The best IRB CZ pair on garnet is QB12 and QB11. Its CZ fidelity is 0.998693 (uncertainty 0.00035). I read it from metrics.irb.cz.slepian_crf.QB12__QB11.fidelity:par=d2 in the default garnet calibration set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade (quality metric set 7e714ed4-d691-43bb-94a5-a4dca1a4979a). That set has 28 CZ pairs, and the runner-up is QB12-QB7 at 0.998016. I ran the Bell circuit H then CX on that pair on garnet:mock with 100 shots. Job 01a15fa3-5295-71f2-aa67-729714e95d3e completed. I checked the transpiled circuit before I submitted it. The only 2-qubit gate acts on QB12 and QB11. Only those two qubits are measured, with QB12 to clbit 0 and QB11 to clbit 1. The counts are {'10': 29, '11': 28, '01': 20, '00': 23}. The bitstrings are Qiskit little-endian, so the left bit is QB11. The counts are spread evenly because the mock returns random results. My first transpile with initial_layout=[QB12, QB11] ignored the layout and put the circuit on QB19 and QB20. An assert stopped that attempt before any job was sent. I fixed it with a full-width circuit that acts directly on the physical indices. The mock used its own calibration set, f04fe114-002f-46bd-8fa4-2a577ff56501.
